title: KDP Cover Requirements: What Most Authors Get Wrong
excerpt: CMYK color, wrong dimensions, and a missing manifest property are the three cover mistakes that trip up KDP authors. Here is how to get your cover right the first time.

meta_description: KDP cover rejected or showing as a gray box? Learn the exact KDP ebook cover requirements — size, color mode, format — and the three mistakes authors make most.
feature_image_alt: A book cover being checked against Amazon KDP dimension and color requirements
html:
A book cover can be beautifully designed and still get rejected by KDP, or worse, go live as a blank gray box on the product page. The reasons are almost always technical, not artistic. This guide covers the exact KDP cover requirements and the three mistakes that catch the most authors.

The KDP ebook cover requirements

For a Kindle ebook, Amazon KDP asks for a cover image that meets these specs:

  • Minimum size: 625 × 1000 pixels.
  • Ideal size: 1600 × 2560 pixels for the sharpest display.
  • Aspect ratio: 1.6:1 (height to width) — a 2:3 shape.
  • File format: JPEG or TIFF.
  • Color mode: RGB.
  • Maximum file size: 50MB.

Note there are two covers in play: the image embedded inside your EPUB, and the separate cover you upload to the KDP product listing. Both need to meet these specs. For the full breakdown across platforms, see our Amazon KDP cover requirements reference.

Mistake 1: Using a print cover in CMYK

This is the most common cover failure. Print covers are designed in CMYK color mode at 300 DPI, because that is what physical printing needs. KDP's ebook system expects RGB and rejects CMYK images — even though the file looks identical to you on screen.

Authors who design a paperback first often reuse the same file for the ebook and hit a wall. The fix is to export a separate RGB JPEG specifically for the ebook, at the correct pixel dimensions. Don't extract the image from a print-ready PDF; start from your design file and export fresh in RGB.

How to check: Run your cover through the free Cover Checker, which flags CMYK color mode, wrong dimensions, and unsupported formats before you upload.

Mistake 2: Wrong dimensions or aspect ratio

Two things go wrong here. The first is size: some older tools and blog posts still cite a 500-pixel minimum, which is outdated. KDP's current minimum is 625 × 1000 pixels, and anything below that displays poorly on modern high-resolution screens.

The second is shape. A square cover or a landscape image gets stretched or letterboxed by KDP's display templates. Start from a canvas with the correct 1.6:1 height-to-width ratio — 1600 × 2560 pixels is the standard working size — so your cover fills the frame without distortion.

Mistake 3: The cover shows as a gray box

This one is sneaky because there is no upload error. Your book goes live, and the cover appears as a blank gray placeholder in both the KDP dashboard and the store listing. The image is inside the EPUB, but the file wasn't declared with properties="cover-image" in the OPF manifest, so the platform can't identify which image is the cover.

The fix is to add that property to the cover's manifest entry. If you built the EPUB with a conversion tool, regenerate it with the cover correctly flagged. For the underlying error, see our reference on the cover image not declared in the OPF manifest.

A quick pre-upload cover routine

  1. Export a fresh RGB JPEG at 1600 × 2560 pixels, separate from any print file.
  2. Run the Cover Checker to confirm dimensions, color mode, and format.
  3. Confirm the manifest property so the cover isn't a gray box on the store page.
  4. Match your metadata — the title and author on the cover must match the KDP form exactly, or the book can be held during review.

Get these three right and your cover uploads cleanly and displays sharply on every Kindle device. Most cover problems are a five-minute export-and-check away from being solved — see the full cover requirements by platform if you also publish to Apple Books or IngramSpark.
